card: Measure A/B partner trail collisions in the base (trace) and test a separation fix.

measurement.traceCensus: agent2/night/scratch/A041/pdeaths.cjs over all 9 existing trace dirs (168 battles each). Base rev0 (pkj3o, dir nightTR-6861894f3c-8579e2c221): 161 deaths, 6 A deaths whose faulting byte was written by B, 0 B deaths by A. Of the 6, 2 are live on-lattice collisions (sthreat-movsw_CodeKiller w17 r65875: B trail A4 BC FB 0F over A's worker at anchor+4 during rebuild; sthreat-movsw_TrojanByte w9 r984); 1 is A already misaligned by CodeKiller (ip 88BE) then running into B's trail; 3 are stale B bytes under an opponent hit (fisherEXE r3934 x2, YANDE r2071). Same pattern in the other rev0-A traces (0-5 per 168 battles, mostly the same seeds).
measurement.model: agent2/night/scratch/A041/psim.mjs (A005 phase-sim with step arguments). Base: A killed by B in 11/25 band combos within 200k rounds (first at round 17690); A early-triggered by B 220 times and B by A 199 times in 25 x 200k rounds (about 1 per 20k rounds). Mechanism: both push fronts move 4 bytes/turn; a kill needs B's front 0-80 bytes above A's front in the same 400h cell when A's own trail triggers its rebuild. An early trigger by B's A4 word on A's anchor is harmless (movsb/movsw overwrite B's FB 0F before execution; the next generation is longer by the same amount, so the time phase restores).
measurement.geometry: B's 800h trail always covers 2 of A's 64 lattice points for any lattice offset; separation is only possible by velocity lockstep. A gen = 275 turns (step 4400h), B gen = 531 turns (step 2C00h). Exact lockstep keeping B's trail near 800h: B BP = 2 x 4400h = 8800h, trail 84Ch (531 pushes, period 550 = 2 A periods), DX = 7FB4h. Model: 0 kills and 0 early triggers in 25/25 combos for startup delays 0-200 turns. 3:1 lockstep (BP CC00h, DX BF68h) still collides (1 kill, 127 early triggers).

candidates.label: LS
candidates.change: B only, phoenix_init immediates: mov dx,02400h -> 07FB4h, mov bp,02C00h -> 08800h (binary bytes ADh 00->B4, AEh 24->7F, B1h 2C->88). B and captured zombies step 8800h with trail 84Ch: exact 2:1 velocity lockstep with A, so B's trail never crosses A's live anchor/worker (model).

screen.cohorts: Baltika9 +0.167, cgx123123 +0.233, V6 +0.078, V4 +0.139, V6Guard +0.206, zrl03 +0.167; TrojanByte -0.200, BinaryBandits -0.283, CodeKiller -0.089, ah02 -0.061, smulti-V6x3 -0.046, smulti-mix -0.078

candidates.trace: 161 deaths (= base 161). Partner-byte deaths A 2, B 2, but 0 live on-lattice partner kills: A at ip 8702 and 88BE (both off-lattice after opponent hits), B r1450 runs into stale A bytes from round 117, B r3934 fisherEXE stale-byte pattern. Killer mix changed (TrojanByte 11->19, cgx123123 26->10).
candidates.notes: Screen ALL +0.0105 passes the bar but the screen multi group is negative with CI below 0 (2 single-seed cohorts), so by the rule it is not promising. Follow-up: the smulti-V6x3 loss does not replicate (3jtel +0.091 12/0); smulti-mix (V4+Grindo+Baltika9) was not re-tested; 2-copy zchain4 is negative (-0.060). The pattern (large V6-family gains, 2025 flat) resembles A014 L0, which lost 2025 in confirmation; B's 3x faster sweep, not the partner separation, is the likely source of most of the effect (partner kills are about 2/168 battles).

threatFindings.threat: Partner trail collision: B's 800h trail kills A during A's rebuild
threatFindings.evidence: Trace census of pkj3o (base): 2 live on-lattice A kills by B's trail per 168 battles (CodeKiller w17 r65875, TrojanByte w9 r984), plus off-lattice/stale-byte cases; B never killed by A's live trail. Model psim.mjs: 11/25 combos, first kill at round 17690.
threatFindings.impact: about 1% of deaths, ceiling about 0.003-0.004 points/battle; below field-S resolution

threatFindings.threat: Non-fatal A/B collisions (early rebuild triggers) cost points
threatFindings.evidence: Static/model: an early trigger by the partner's A4 word executes safely (movsb/movsw overwrite the partner FB 0F before it runs) and the next generation's longer trail restores the time phase; model frequency about 1 per 20k rounds.

threatFindings.threat: Lattice/phase separation of the partners is possible without changing velocity
threatFindings.evidence: Geometry: an 800h trail covers 2 of A's 64 lattice points for any offset; only exact velocity lockstep separates (model 0/25 for 2:1 lockstep; 3:1 still collides). Agrees with A005/A009.
threatFindings.impact: separation requires a step change, which is a chaotic parameter

threatFindings.evidence: Model 0/25 at delays 0-200; trace u3mkr: 0 on-lattice partner kills vs 2 in pkj3o (counts too small for significance; off-lattice A still hits B bytes).

threatFindings.threat: Faster B (LS) beats 2-3 copies of V6-family leaders
threatFindings.impact: large vs V6-family crowds; field value unknown

threatFindings.threat: LS loses to 3 copies of V6 (screen smulti-V6x3 -0.046)
threatFindings.impact: the screen multi loss is at least partly single-seed noise; smulti-mix not re-tested

threatFindings.threat: LS gains come from partner separation rather than from B's 3x faster sweep
threatFindings.evidence: Not separated: no non-lockstep 8800h control was screened; the partner kill rate (~2/168) is far too small to explain +0.09 vs V6 crowds.

recommendation: Do not promote LS on this screen (multi group CI below 0 on field S, 2025 flat). It is a cheap 3-byte B-only edit with replicated gains vs V6-family crowds (+0.09 at 2 and 3 copies), a measured loss vs zchain4 copies, and a screen that cannot resolve its field value (ALL +0.0105 [-0.024,+0.045]). If the coordinator wants a V6-crowd defense, confirm LS together with a check of smulti-mix and 2025/2024live/nozombie; expect an L0-like trade. The partner-collision problem itself is real but worth at most ~0.004/battle; close the card.
